title: Removable Discontinuity and Function Extension
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine where f(x) = (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) is discontinuous. Classify the discontinuity and define f(2) to make the extended function continuous at x = 2.

steps.title: Check Domain and Continuity Conditions
steps.explanation: The denominator is zero at x = 2, so f(2) is undefined.
steps.why: Condition 1 of continuity fails because f(2) does not exist.

steps.title: Compute the Limit as x Approaches 2
steps.explanation: Factor the difference of squares and cancel (x - 2) to evaluate the limit.
steps.why: The limit exists and equals 4, proving the discontinuity is removable.

steps.title: Construct the Continuous Extension
steps.explanation: Define the value at x = 2 to match the limiting value 4.
steps.why: Setting F(2) equal to the limit satisfies lim F(x) = F(2).
